title: The Flavor of Green Tea over Rice (1952)

commenti.body:
>Despite its age, it quietly promotes fighting against generational traumas and identifies existence of the generational gap.

That's part and parcel of Ozu's work dating back to well before The Flavor of Green Tea Over Rice. Ozu's handling of these issues feels so much more complete and nuanced that what you get in a lot of modern films, which are often very lacking when trying to cover these issues. The Only Son probably being the best example of how expertly Ozu could tackle things like generational gaps and trauma. The themes of that film feel more relevant today than ever.


For me, I would actually place it slightly above An Autumn Afternoon. Both are fantastic films, but I don't think I would consider either go be top 10 Ozu films personally.
